blocks.text: Lots and land in Simon Fraser Univer.
The UniverCity tenure record

items.t: How the land was created, as the Trust states it: the land remains under SFU ownership: SFU Community Trust (SFU's trustee corporation) leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold. The servicing and subdivision happened at the Trust-to-developer level — a buyer never buys one of those parcels; the parcels become strata developments.

What a buyer actually holds: a leasehold prepaid strata interest — the strata lot plus the remaining term of the 99-year ground lease. A current Origin listing states the structure in terms: "Leasehold expires in 2109" (9150 University High Street).

No fee-simple lots inside UniverCity: directly — there are no conventional fee-simple residential lots inside UniverCity itself: every market home is a strata unit on SFU's 99-year prepaid ground lease, so "lot size" comparisons between buildings come down to unit size, floor and outlook rather than land.
SFU student residences and campus housing are not market housing: and are not land stock in any form.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: Simon Fraser Univer. is the top of Burnaby Mountain in the City of Burnaby: the Simon Fraser University (SFU) Burnaby campus and the UniverCity residential community beside it. The board sub-area is listed as "Simon Fraser Univer."; SnapStats prints the full name as "Simon Fraser University SFU." A separate neighbouring sub-area, "Simon Fraser Hills," covers the Forest Grove side of the mountain and is not this area.
Nearby areas: Westridge, Lochdale, Sperling-Duthie (via Gaglardi Way), Forest Grove / Simon Fraser Hills, and Port Moody and Coquitlam across the mountain's east side.

What UniverCity is: a planned residential community next to the SFU campus. In 1996 the City of Burnaby approved the Official Community Plan and zoning amendments for it; the OCP envisions a dense, mixed-use community on about 65 hectares, allowing up to 4,536 residential units in two neighbourhoods south and east of campus, housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out, built out in four neighbourhoods — West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes.

Schools (SD41, Ministry-listed names): University Highlands Elementary is the elementary school inside UniverCity (LEED Gold certified; the school notes most families can walk to it in under 5 minutes); Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive) is the public secondary school on the mountain. The one locator run documented is for 8800 Eastlake Drive: Cameron Elementary (K–7) / Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12).

Transit: TransLink's R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at the SFU Exchange (at least every 10 minutes at peak, 15 minutes off-peak to Burrard Station); the 145 bus connects SFU Exchange to Production Way–University Station on the Millennium Line. The proposed Burnaby Mountain Gondola (about seven minutes, Production Way–University Station to near the SFU bus exchange) is not yet approved or funded per TransLink.

Setting: the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area surrounding the campus and community covers 578 hectares, with 34 multi-use trails over 28 kilometres, climbing from about 25 metres above sea level to the 366-metre summit; SFU transferred more than 320 hectares to the City for the conservation area as part of the original arrangement. Shopping is centred on University High Street in the Cornerstone/High Street core.

Burnaby community — Detached median $1,825,000, $662/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 37 DOM; Condos & Townhomes median $686,000, $763/sq ft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 DOM. SnapStats publishes no SFU sub-area median, and none of these figures describes land.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: The ground lease is the governing document (this area's first rule): SFU Community Trust leases parcels to developers on 99-year leases and the land remains SFU's. Before anything else, confirm the lease commencement date, remaining term, whether rent is prepaid for the full term, and any rent-review or end-of-term provisions — the lease, not the building, is what a buyer's lender and lawyer will scrutinize.

City plan and zoning: citywide direction is the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP Bylaw); UniverCity is governed by its own OCP framework from the 1996 approvals (up to 4,536 units on about 65 hectares).
SSMUH position: No SSMUH unit count for an SFU-ground lot is asserted here.

Strata frame (the form every UniverCity purchase actually takes): a UniverCity strata is still a strata corporation under the Strata Property Act, so Form B diligence under s. 59 applies (fees, amounts owing, special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement and depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page) — read alongside the ground lease, which the Form B does not answer. Depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for strata corporations with 5 or more lots since July 1, 2024; at least 10% of the annual operating budget to the CRF since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (the rule governs strata bylaws, not the SFU ground lease itself); only 55+ age bylaws are valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions), a "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw, and no UniverCity building is confirmed to carry a 55+ bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no SFU-ground ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error, and it is not asserted for this ground.

Burnaby property taxes (2026): City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

No Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in Burnaby: the EHT is a City of Vancouver tax (3%) and does not apply here — stated expressly because this sub-area's university name invites the confusion; it also does not apply on UEL/university-vw ground, which is a different ground in any case.

blocks.text: Good to know about Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: The lease expiry is printed in listings, if you look: a current Origin listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109" in its body copy — the ground-lease term is a searchable, comparable fact between buildings, and the oldest (early-2000s) and newest buildings do not carry the same remaining term.

The elementary school beside you may not be your catchment school: the SD41 locator returns Cameron Elementary for 8800 Eastlake Drive — Burnaby Mountain Secondary's own address — even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity a short walk away. Listing copy that states catchments is copy, not a locator run.

The community was planned whole: UniverCity's OCP allows up to 4,536 units housing up to 10,000 residents on about 65 hectares in neighbourhoods south and east of campus — the "still building out" feel (Arbour in the Slopes is the current phase) is the 1996 plan working as approved, on land the Trust still owns.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw in 2026: Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and replaced the 1965 bylaw (No. 4742) outright — any older source citing the 1965 bylaw for UniverCity or an edge-pocket lot is citing a repealed bylaw.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: streets and boundaries

items.t: This area is the top of Burnaby Mountain: the Simon Fraser University (SFU) Burnaby campus and the UniverCity residential community beside it, reached by Burnaby Mountain Parkway and Gaglardi Way.
UniverCity occupies about 65 hectares south and east of the campus, in neighbourhoods the developer materials name West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes.
The campus and community are ringed by the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area, whose trails climb from about 25 metres above sea level to the 366-metre summit.
The board sub-area name is printed in full as "Simon Fraser University SFU"; the neighbouring sub-area "Simon Fraser Hills" covers the Forest Grove side of the mountain and is a different area.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: the housing stock

items.t: Almost every home here is a strata condominium or townhome in UniverCity, because the community was planned as a dense, mixed-use development rather than a lot subdivision.

There are no conventional fee-simple residential lots inside UniverCity itself: buyers own their strata unit on SFU's prepaid ground lease, so comparisons between buildings come down to unit size, floor and outlook rather than land.
An early anchor project is The Hub at UniverCity, completed in spring 2009 with 146 condominium units and 23,000 square feet of retail space including the grocery store on University High Street.
Intergulf Development Group's own materials list its earlier mountain buildings as Novo 1 and Novo 2, The Peak (2019) and Terraces at The Peak (2020), before its current Arbour project in the Slopes.
Detached houses are rare in this sub-area and sit mainly in pockets at the mountain's edges.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Tenure is the rule that defines buying here: the land remains under SFU ownership, and SFU Community Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold.

The community's density is set by its own Official Community Plan (OCP) framework: the City of Burnaby approved the OCP and zoning amendments in 1996, allowing up to 4,536 residential units housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out.

As part of that arrangement, SFU transferred more than 320 hectares of university land to the City of Burnaby for the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area, which is why the built area is small and the protected forest around it is permanent.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Burnaby Mountain Park at the summit holds the Centennial Rose Garden, the Kamui Mintara (Playground of the Gods) sculptures, a playground and picnic areas.

Childcare is on the mountain: SFU Community Trust's community contact list confirms the UniverCity Childcare Centre and the Verdant Early Childhood Centre operate in UniverCity alongside SFU Childcare services.
The public secondary school on the mountain is Burnaby Mountain Secondary, 8800 Eastlake Drive, operated by School District 41.

City recreation programs run out of a school here: the community association lists City of Burnaby fitness and recreation programs for all ages at University Highlands Elementary, with occasional events at Richard Bolton Park.
Shopping is centred on University High Street, where The Hub's retail includes the community grocery store, pharmacy and café space beside the residential buildings.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: development and new projects

items.t: Arbour at SFU, 9688 University Crescent, Intergulf Development Group: 178 homes in 4 buildings — 1, 2 and 3 bedroom condominiums and 3 bedroom stacked townhomes — in UniverCity's Slopes neighbourhood, beside the new roughly 30,000-square-foot Slopes Neighbourhood Park.
Burnaby Mountain Gondola, TransLink: proposed straight-line gondola from Production Way–University Station to a terminal near the SFU bus exchange.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: getting around

items.t: The R5 Hastings Street RapidBus terminates at SFU Exchange, linking the mountain to Burrard Station downtown at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak.
The 145 bus is the SkyTrain link, running between SFU Exchange and Production Way–University Station on the Millennium Line.
The 144 bus connects the mountain to Metrotown Station via Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, and the 143 connects SFU to Burquitlam Station, per TransLink's Burnaby system map.
There is no SkyTrain station on the mountain itself; every rail trip starts with a bus down Burnaby Mountain Parkway or Gaglardi Way.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the building's ground lease before anything else: confirm the lease commencement date, the remaining term and any end-of-term provisions in the SFU Community Trust lease structure, because tenure, not the building, is the long-term risk in UniverCity.
Do not price a unit as if the gondola exists: TransLink states it is not approved or funded, so current transit value is the R5 and bus network only.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Simon Fraser University Area?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 6 houses and 81 condos and townhomes listed in Simon Fraser University Area. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Simon Fraser University Area a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes had 7% (a buyers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Simon Fraser University Area from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 1 house and 36 condos and townhomes sold in Simon Fraser University Area over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in August with 1 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 9 sold.

faq.q: How big is Simon Fraser University Area compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In October 2026, Simon Fraser University Area held 1.4% of the 430 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 6.2% of the 1,309 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Simon Fraser University Area?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 6.9% of the 87 homes listed in Simon Fraser University Area and condos and townhomes made up 93.1%; of the 6 that sold, houses were 0.0% and condos and townhomes 100.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Simon Fraser University Area than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 8 in June to 6 in October 2026 (−25.0%); condos and townhomes fell from 94 in June to 81 in October 2026 (−13.8%).

faq.q: Can I buy a lot — freehold land — at SFU / UniverCity?
faq.a: No. There are no conventional fee-simple residential lots inside UniverCity: SFU Community Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers on 99-year leases, and every market home is a leasehold strata unit on that structure.

faq.q: So what do I own when I buy at UniverCity?
faq.a: A strata lot and a leasehold interest for the remaining term of the 99-year prepaid ground lease — one current listing states its building's lease expires in 2109. You do not own the land under the building.

faq.q: What should I read first — the Form B or the ground lease?
faq.a: Both, in that order of risk: the Form B for the strata's finances and bylaws, and the ground lease for commencement date, remaining term, prepaid status and end-of-term provisions. The lease is what a lender and lawyer will scrutinize; some lenders cap mortgage terms against the remaining lease term.

faq.q: Is Arbour a chance to buy a lot in the Slopes?
faq.a: No — Arbour (9688 University Crescent) is a 178-home leasehold condominium and stacked-townhome presale.

faq.q: Are there any detached lots for sale on the mountain?
faq.a: No named bare-land subdivision or vacant-lot offering on those edges was verified.

faq.q: Are the UniverCity buildings freehold strata?
faq.a: A buyer owns the strata lot and a lease interest, not the land — and none of them is duplex stock.

faq.q: Does the gondola change what I should pay?
faq.a: No — TransLink states the Burnaby Mountain Gondola is not yet approved or funded; treat it as upside, not as current transit, when pricing a unit.

faq.q: Which Burnaby zoning bylaw is current?
faq.a: Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815 — adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026.

faq.q: Are UniverCity homes freehold or leasehold?
faq.a: Leasehold. SFU Community Trust's history states the land remains under SFU ownership and parcels are leased to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so a buyer purchases a leasehold strata interest in the home, not the land under it. Read the ground lease for the building — its start date, remaining term and end-of-term provisions — before subject removal, because the lease is what a lender and a lawyer will examine first.

faq.q: Is the Burnaby Mountain Gondola built, or even approved?
faq.a: Neither. TransLink states the gondola is not yet approved or funded: it must be included in a future investment plan and approved by the TransLink Board and the Mayors' Council on Regional Transportation. The preferred route is a straight line from Production Way–University Station to a terminal near the SFU bus exchange, with trips of about seven minutes for the roughly 25,000 daily trips the mountain generates.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves a UniverCity address?
faq.a: University Highlands Elementary, 9388 Tower Road, is the School District 41 (Burnaby) school inside the community, and SFU's schools page notes most homes were located so families can walk to it in under five minutes.

faq.q: How do residents get downtown without a car?
faq.a: By RapidBus and bus-to-SkyTrain connections. TransLink's R5 Hastings Street RapidBus terminates at the SFU Exchange and links the mountain to Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver, running at least every 10 minutes at peak and every 15 minutes off-peak, and the 145 bus connects SFU Exchange to Production Way–University Station on the Millennium Line.

faq.q: What did condos in Simon Fraser University SFU sell for?
faq.a: 87 condos sold in Simon Fraser University SFU between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $512,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Simon Fraser University SFU?
faq.a: The median was 39 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.8% of the last list price (8% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
